question: How sensitive is isolated PP_5317 deletion growth to a hypothetical external 4HBZ supply, and does the existing model permit donor secretion without adding transport?
decision_rule: No reaction, gene assignment, biomass demand or historical medium definition is changed. Do not rescore the fitness benchmark or call hypothetical supply a correction. Preserve every result and failed attempt. Require independently agreeing solver objectives and primal certificates; failure never means zero growth.
interpretation_limits: No extracellular precursor concentration, donor secretion rate, mutant-specific uptake rate, or observed cross-feeding is established by this diagnostic.
Uptake/secretion units are mmol/gDW/h, not medium concentration. Population composition, biomass and elapsed time are unavailable for a concentration conversion.
Minimum uptake holds the mutant at a specified fraction of parental model growth and forbids simultaneous net secretion; this is a diagnostic LP, not a new physiological growth model.

A 4HBZ carbon-source condition is excluded from trace-uptake optimization because reducing its uptake would also remove the main carbon substrate. Coumarate conditions remain included as natural precursor-supply controls.
Donor secretion is maximized while retaining at least 95% of parental model growth. It establishes possible flux under inherited assumptions without regulation, not secretion that occurs in cells.
Pooled transposon relative fitness is not identical to isolated complete-gene-deletion growth; exact generations, insertion-specific effects and metabolite exchange remain unresolved.
Inherited PpnP/quinone/donor/maintenance assumptions persist; ATP maintenance lower bound is zero.
Energy tests close all boundaries, so the two energy contexts are not independent tests of metabolite sharing.
